title: ATiM: Autotuning Tensor Programs for Processing-in-DRAM
problem: Current software stacks for DRAM-PIM (specifically UPMEM) rely on hand-tuned libraries, lack high-level programming abstractions, and have no systematic optimization framework, making it difficult to achieve peak hardware utilization for tensor workloads including LLM layers.
motivation: Processing-in-DRAM can dramatically reduce memory bandwidth pressure for LLM inference, but poor programmability and absence of autotuning compilers leave substantial performance on the table.
method: ATiM automatically optimizes tensor programs (matrix calculations) for UPMEM systems, which perform computation inside memory chips rather than in the main processor. It searches different ways of organizing code that runs on the main processor and the code that runs inside the memory chips, using techniques designed for UPMEM's structure where memory is organized into separate banks. The system explores different choices like how many parallel workers to use, how to break up loops, and where to place data in memory, then generates optimized code without requiring manual library engineering.
key_novelty: ATiM is the first compiler that automatically searches for and generates optimized tensor program code for UPMEM systems, handling their banked-memory structure without requiring engineers to manually write libraries.
contributions: Automated joint search over host and kernel tensor program space for UPMEM
PIM-aware optimizations for efficient boundary condition handling in banked DRAM layouts
Improved search algorithms tailored to UPMEM's expanded design space
Up to 6.18x speedup on UPMEM benchmark kernels and 8.21x on GPT-J layers over hand-tuned baselines

metrics.speedup: Up to 6.18x on UPMEM benchmark kernels; 8.21x on GPT-J layers

limitations: Evaluation is limited to UPMEM hardware; generalizability to other DRAM-PIM architectures (e.g., HBM-PIM) is not demonstrated.
